name: Direct medial approach to the distal tibia
corridor: Direct subperiosteal medial exposure centered on a vertical medial split-depression fragment, with optional proximal MIPO extension

positioning.text: Position supine with the leg externally rotated enough for direct medial access and maintain unobstructed AP, lateral, and mortise imaging.

setup.text: Confirm soft-tissue readiness, map medial impaction and osteochondral fragments on CT, and choose direct versus limited/MIPO plate application.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark medial tibial border, medial malleolus, ankle joint, saphenous vein and nerve course, and the proximal exit of the medial fracture line.

incision.text: Center the medial incision over the split fragment and extend proximally only enough to displace, reduce, and fix it or create a safe MIPO plate tunnel.

superficial_interval.text: Raise a full-thickness medial flap while identifying and protecting the saphenous vein and nerve.

deep_interval.text: Expose the vertical medial fragment directly, mobilize it enough to enter the joint, elevate adjacent plafond impaction, and preserve remaining periosteal attachments.

layers.text: Skin, saphenous neurovascular plane, medial periosteum, vertical fracture plane, then medial plafond and joint.

structures_encountered.text: Saphenous vein and nerve, medial tibial periosteum, medial split fragment, osteochondral fragments, impacted plafond, and talar dome are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Medial skin envelope, saphenous vein and nerve, periosteal fragment blood supply, posterior tibial structures with posterior extension, and articular cartilage are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Avoid placing bulky hardware directly beneath a compromised medial incision and avoid circumferential stripping of the split fragment.

retraction_hazards.text: Use limited atraumatic retraction; excessive flap tension or posterior dissection risks wound failure and neurovascular injury.

exposure.text: Provides direct visualization of a vertical medial split, medial plafond impaction, and associated osteochondral fragments.

limitations.text: Exposure is fracture-specific and does not adequately address dominant anterolateral or posterior plafond pathology through the same incision.

extensions.text: Extend proximally for direct medial plating only when soft tissues permit; otherwise combine limited articular exposure with percutaneous proximal plate insertion.

indications.text: Use for vertical medial split-depression pilon fractures with medial comminution, impaction, or an independent osteochondral fragment.

relative_contraindications.text: Choose an anteromedial or other fragment-directed approach when medial skin is tenuous or a plate directly under the incision would be unsafe.

implant_implications.text: A medial buttress plate may be applied directly or passed proximally using MIPO; position hardware to avoid incision pressure and saphenous structures.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Use AP, lateral, mortise, and oblique views to confirm elevation of impaction, medial buttress alignment, joint congruity, and screw containment.

closure.text: Restore periosteal coverage where possible and close the viable medial skin without tension or implant prominence beneath the incision.

complications.text: Complications include wound necrosis, infection, saphenous neuritis, symptomatic hardware, malreduction, nonunion, stiffness, and post-traumatic arthritis.

bailouts.text: Convert the proximal portion to percutaneous plate insertion or select a separate fragment-directed window if direct extension would compromise medial skin.

procedure_applications.condition: A vertical medial split-depression fracture with medial articular impaction requires direct elevation and buttress fixation

questions.question: What fracture morphology favors this approach?
questions.answer: A vertical medial split-depression fracture with medial articular impaction.

questions.question: What reduces proximal soft-tissue disruption?
questions.answer: Limited articular exposure combined with minimally invasive proximal plate insertion.
